t: Congress voted for independence on 2 July 1776 and approved the wording of the Declaration on 4 July; Thomas Jefferson wrote most of the first draft, and Congress cut nearly a fourth of it.
It gave the political, moral and legal grounds for independence, citing 27 grievances against King George III and asserting natural and legal rights, including a right of revolution.
Little noticed in the years after the Revolution, it gained a second life from the 1790s and was later invoked by abolitionists, women's rights campaigners, Abraham Lincoln and many new states.
dyk: Jefferson's draft charged King George III with forcing the slave trade on the colonies, but Congress struck the passage out, in part to appease South Carolina and Georgia, which had significant involvement in the slave trade. Jefferson later wrote that Congress had 'mangled' his draft.
ev: The American Revolutionary War begins in April with the battles of Lexington and Concord, and the Second Continental Congress meets in Philadelphia in May
On 11 June Congress appoints the Committee of Five, and Jefferson writes the first draft between 11 and 28 June
On 2 July Congress adopts the resolution of independence, and on 4 July it approves the final wording of the Declaration and sends it to the printer
John Dunlap's broadsides are read in public on 8 July in Philadelphia, Trenton and Easton, and most delegates sign the engrossed copy on 2 August
A facsimile of the engrossed copy is made, and it becomes the basis of most modern reproductions
The Seneca Falls Convention issues a Declaration of Sentiments patterned on the Declaration, with the words 'all men and women are created equal'
Abraham Lincoln makes the Declaration the centrepiece of his Gettysburg Address
The engrossed Declaration is transferred to the National Archives, where it is on permanent display

f.made: Drafted largely by Thomas Jefferson between 11 and 28 June 1776 for the Committee of Five, then edited and adopted by the Second Continental Congress; the signed copy was engrossed by the clerk Timothy Matlack
f.form: A political and legal statement, often discussed as five parts: introduction, preamble, indictment of King George III, denunciation of the British people and conclusion; it lists 27 grievances against the king
f.where: The signed, engrossed copy is on display at the National Archives in Washington, D.C.; two Dunlap broadsides are kept in the Library of Congress
f.known: The words 'all men are created equal'; 'Life, Liberty and the pursuit of Happiness'; Jefferson's drafting; the 27 grievances; the Dunlap broadside; John Hancock's signature; the struck-out passage on the slave trade; its later use by reform movements
